description:
Create a lightweight architecture decision record (ADR) describing when Pulse RSS should remain on htmx/server-rendered templates vs adopt a client framework (e.g., React) for specific surfaces.

Scope:
- Add a decision doc in repository docs that includes:
  - Current architecture summary (Go templates + htmx + modular vanilla JS).
  - Explicit trigger criteria for framework adoption (measurable thresholds such as client-state complexity, component reuse pressure, SPA routing/data-cache needs, team onboarding costs, and test burden).
  - Non-goals and anti-triggers (cases where framework migration is unnecessary).
  - Preferred incremental path (islands/targeted adoption) if criteria are met.
  - Re-evaluation cadence and owner.
- Keep guidance practical so future agents can make consistent decisions.

Acceptance criteria:
- ADR is committed with concrete, measurable criteria (not generic pros/cons only).
- Doc includes at least one example scenario that would trigger adoption and one that would not.
- References current file/module layout after ac7dd48 refactor.

Handoff notes:
- This issue is strategic/backlog; it should not block functional frontend work.
title: Document criteria for adopting a frontend framework

description:
Refactor app_js_test.go away from broad source-token assertions toward behavior-oriented and structure-aware checks.

Context:
- Current tests read JS source files and assert many literal strings. This creates false positives/negatives during safe refactors and module extraction.

Scope:
- Audit app_js_test.go and classify assertions into: keep, rewrite, or remove.
- Replace brittle literal checks with tests that verify observable outcomes where feasible (server output, script loading contract, integration behavior already covered elsewhere).
- For checks that must remain source-based, narrow them to stable contracts (e.g., entrypoint import, critical selector presence) and avoid asserting incidental implementation details.
- Reduce duplicate assertions and align messages with current behavior.

Acceptance criteria:
- Test file has materially fewer implementation-detail string checks.
- Remaining assertions are stable and intentional, with clear failure messages.
- No loss of coverage for critical frontend wiring expectations.
- ./scripts/check.sh passes.

Handoff notes:
- Coordinate with the smoke-test issue so this file does not become the only frontend safety net.

description:
Create an automated smoke suite for high-value UI interactions so frontend refactors are safer.

Scope:
- Add a minimal browser-level test harness that runs in CI/local with deterministic setup.
- Cover at least these user flows end-to-end:
  1) Select a feed and confirm items load into #main-content.
  2) Expand/collapse an item with content.
  3) Toggle read/unread and verify row state updates.
  4) Keyboard navigation sanity: j/k movement and h/l panel navigation in desktop layout.
- Use project conventions (Go-first if practical) and keep dependencies lightweight.

Implementation guidance:
- Prefer stable selectors already present in templates (IDs/data-attributes) over brittle text matching.
- Keep fixtures/data setup reproducible so tests are not network-dependent.
- If new tooling is needed, document why and add scripts/docs so another agent can run it easily.

Acceptance criteria:
- New smoke tests run locally with a single command (documented in repo).
- Tests are deterministic and pass in current environment.
- ./scripts/check.sh remains green.

Handoff notes:
- If full keyboard-flow automation is flaky, keep the suite minimal and reliable, then file a linked follow-up issue for deeper keyboard coverage.
